I farm 10.7 mu in a wheat-maize rotation, so I will use the same 10.7 mu for winter wheat first and then summer maize after wheat harvest. I am 65 and I have farmed for 30 years, so I will keep to a steady, familiar way that protects yield and does not make the work too complicated. I have well irrigation, so I will rely on that to secure the key water stages. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most of the fertilizer in before sowing, irrigate at the important stages, and keep pesticide use limited to what is needed for weeds and disease. After wheat harvest, I will plant hybrid maize on the same land because hybrid maize gives me more stable yield. I will keep fertilizer moderate, use fewer irrigations than wheat, and control pests when pressure shows up. I will use rotary tillage for wheat to prepare the land well, and no-tillage for maize after wheat harvest to save time and catch the season on time.
